description: Cross-language golden matrix for Script Delivery v1 (docs/proposals/script-delivery.md). Every envelope is produced by the TypeScript signer in @sqlite-host/authoring and verified by SqliteHost.Delivery in C#. tests/delivery-golden/run.mjs rebuilds each envelope from its `build` block and byte-compares it against the committed file (regenerate with UPDATE_DELIVERY_GOLDENS=1); the C# DeliveryGoldenTests read `envelope`, `nowUnixMs`, `outcome` and `expect` and ignore `build`. Both sides must agree, which is the point: bytes signed by Node must verify under .NET and nowhere else.

cases.why: The happy path, and the byte-for-byte cross-language contract: the verified payload must equal the committed script fixture exactly, so the runtime's existing JSON parsing sees bytes unchanged by the delivery layer.

hmac-sha256 with both optional fields absent. Proves empty expiresAt means `never expires` (not `expired at epoch 0`) and empty minApiLevel means `unspecified` (not `0`) — an absent-vs-zero confusion here would silently reject every long-lived script.
A genuinely signed envelope past its TTL. The signature is valid, so reaching `expired` also proves the expiry check runs after signature verification, not instead of it.
Correctly signed by the real private key but claiming a kid this build does not trust — the shape of a key that was rotated out. Must not fall back to `try every key`.

A well-formed envelope claiming a TRUSTED kid but signed with a private key the client never trusted — i.e. a forgery attempt, not a corrupted download. This is the single most important negative case: it is what an attacker who can serve bytes will actually try.

valid-rsa with a single payload byte flipped and payloadLength left intact, so every framing check still passes. Only the signature can catch it — which is exactly the property the whole format exists to provide.

valid-rsa rewritten to claim hmac-sha256 — the JWT `alg confusion` attack. Rejected as unknown-key at key selection, because keys are selected by the (kid, alg) PAIR: dev-rsa-1 exists, but not as an HMAC key. It never reaches signature verification.

An algorithm a future signer might use (rsa-pss-sha256) that this build does not implement. Must report unsupported-version, not malformed: the operational answer is `ship an app update`, not `retry the download`.
A deliveryVersion this build does not implement. Fails closed on an unknown version instead of guessing the v1 layout.

valid-rsa with the header line endings rewritten to CRLF, as a naive proxy or text-mode file copy would. Must fail loud as malformed rather than as a mysterious bad-signature, so an integrator can tell a broken transport from an attack.
